name: Comoros
sources: World Bank figures in this file were read off IndexMundi's republication of the WDI series named, because api.worldbank.org and data.worldbank.org returned a WAF block page to this session throughout. The full provenance caveat is written out once, in madagascar.json, and applies here identically. MORE OF THIS FILE IS BRACKETED THAN ANY OTHER ON THIS BRANCH, and the four bracketed figures say so individually. A microstate of 412,000 people that had its head of state assassinated five weeks before the game opens is exactly the case the roster's rule about admitted gaps was written for.

GDP $0.43bn: World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.CD, series COM, 1990 = 429,622,100. On 411,598 people that is about $1,044 a head. The economy is vanilla, ylang-ylang and cloves - the Comoros produced most of the world's ylang-ylang, which is a perfume ingredient, so the country's export earnings depended on the French fragrance industry to a degree that is hard to overstate - plus French budget support and remittances from Marseille.

Population 0.412m: World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series COM, 1990 = 411,598. Excludes Mayotte, whose 1991 census counted 94,410 people; that is the correct exclusion for this field and the corresponding claim is on the roster row.

GDP growth for context: World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.KD.ZG, series COM, reads 2.69 in 1988, -3.18 in 1989, 5.09 in 1990, -5.40 in 1991, 8.53 in 1992. Not entered anywhere - recorded because a swing of that amplitude on a base this small is the shape of the whole problem: one cyclone or one bad vanilla price is a recession here.

TFP trend 0.000: entered at zero and flagged as a judgement rather than a reading. There is no Comorian TFP estimate worth citing. Zero is the honest placeholder for an economy whose measured output moves plus or minus five points a year on weather and commodity prices, which had no manufacturing to speak of, and whose real income per head in 2000 was below its 1990 level. Set below Cape Verde's 0.004 and above Madagascar's -0.005.

Inflation 3.0%: NOT SOURCED and flagged as an admitted gap. World Bank FP.CPI.TOTL.ZG has no Comorian entry before 2001, whose first print is 5.55. 0.03 is entered on the franc-zone argument: the Comorian franc was pegged to the French franc at 50:1 under the monetary agreement of 1979, the Banque Centrale des Comores operated an operations account with the French Treasury on the same terms as the BCEAO's, and franc-zone members therefore imported a French price level. Senegal's SOURCED 1990 print in this roster is 0.33% and Cameroon's is comparably low; the Comoros is entered materially above them because it is an island importing nearly all of its food, which the mainland members are not. It is a bracket. Nobody should cite it.

Interest rate 10%: NOT SOURCED and flagged. FR.INR.LEND has no Comorian entry before 1999, whose first print is 13.67. 0.10 is entered as a franc-zone discount rate bracket on the same basis senegal.json uses for the BCEAO, adjusted down slightly for the smaller BCC. The loader's coupled check reads 0.025 - (0.10 - 0.03) = -0.045, comfortably inside the band, so this entry does not do much work in the model - which is fortunate, because it is the weakest number here after the inflation figure it is paired with.

Revenue 14% of GDP: NOT SOURCED - GC.REV.XGRT.GD.ZS has no Comorian entry for this period - and entered as a bracket a little below Cameroon's sourced 14.3% and well below Mauritius's 22.5%. A state that could not reliably pay its civil servants, and whose recurrent budget was topped up by France under the cooperation agreements. Flagged.

Military 1.2% of GDP: NOT SOURCED and flagged. MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS has no Comorian entry for 1990. 1.2% of a $430m economy is about $5m, which is entered as an order-of-magnitude bracket for what the Presidential Guard cost - and the reason it cannot be read off a defence budget is that the Guard was not entirely paid out of one. It was roughly 500 to 700 men commanded by the French mercenary Bob Denard, and a substantial part of its funding came from South Africa, which had bought a friendly government in the Mozambique Channel and an air link that evaded the continental overflight ban. A defence expenditure that a foreign intelligence service pays for does not appear in the country's accounts, and this figure should be read as the low end.

Investment 11% state / 7% private, summing to 18% of GDP: World Bank NE.GDI.TOTL.ZS, series COM, 1990 = 18.04, gross capital formation. The split is APPORTIONED and sums to the sourced total, weighted to the state because almost all of it was donor-financed public works.
Debt 43.1% of GDP: World Bank DT.DOD.DECT.GN.ZS, series COM, 1990 = 43.09, external debt stocks as a share of GNI. Sourced, and one of only two solidly sourced macro ratios in this file.

System Market: the Comoros is entered as Market and it is the loosest of the four system calls on this branch. Ahmed Abdallah's Union Comorienne pour le Progres was the sole legal party from 1982, which points the other way - but there was no plan, no nationalised commanding heights and no state trading monopoly. What there was, was a state too weak to run anything: the vanilla and ylang-ylang trade was in private hands, largely those of a handful of French and Comorian families, and the government's economic function was to collect an export tax and receive French aid. A weak market economy rather than a directed one.

Stability 30 and authoritarianism 0.58: THE LOWEST STABILITY ON THIS BRANCH AND ONE OF THE LOWEST IN THE ROSTER, and January 1990 is the reason. President Ahmed Abdallah was shot dead in his office on the night of 26 November 1989 by members of the Presidential Guard; Bob Denard, who commanded that Guard and had installed Abdallah by landing on the beach in 1978, took control of the islands and then handed them over to French and South African pressure and flew out to Pretoria on 15 December 1989. When the game opens the country has been independent for fourteen years and has had four coups in them, an interim president in Said Mohamed Djohar, French troops on the ground, and a presidential election due in March. Authoritarianism 0.58 is set above Mexico's dominant-party 0.52 and below Cape Verde's 0.62, because the single-party law was collapsing rather than being enforced: the presidential election of 4 and 11 March 1990 was genuinely contested and went to a runoff. THIS PLACES THE COMOROS FRACTIONALLY UNDER government.rs's ELECTORAL_CEILING OF 0.60, AND THAT IS A DELIBERATE, STATED CALL RATHER THAN AN ACCIDENT OF ROUNDING. The consequence is that the model treats the Comoros as a nation that can be removed by a vote and honours the March 1990 date in its Polity block. The alternative reading - that a state run for six weeks by the mercenary who had just killed its president is not an electoral one - is respectable, and a QA reader who moves this to 0.62 should move the Polity's `next` to (0, 0) in the same commit.

Separatism 0.25: THE HIGHEST ON THIS BRANCH AND HIGHER THAN SPAIN'S 0.10, which is the correct ordering and needs saying. This is a state of three islands whose fourth voted to stay French, whose constitution had been rewritten repeatedly over how much autonomy Anjouan and Moheli would get, and where the resentment of Grande Comore's dominance was the standing fact of politics. Anjouan and Moheli both declared independence in 1997 and Anjouan had to be retaken by an African Union force in 2008. Nothing here schedules that; 0.25 states the strain that produced it.

Military strength 0.2: level with Mauritius's, at the roster floor, and for the opposite reason - Mauritius has no army because it has never needed one, and the Comoros has no army because its army is somebody else's. The Presidential Guard was 500 to 700 men under a French mercenary; the Force Comorienne de Defense that nominally existed beside it was smaller and worse. The state's actual security guarantee in January 1990 is the French detachment, and that is expressed in relations rather than here.

Claim on France, share 0.001: Mayotte, argued in full on the roster row. The most consequential single fact about Comorian foreign policy and the one that makes the dyad strange: Moroni holds a claim, endorsed almost annually by the UN General Assembly since 1976, against the only power that will defend it.

pop_growth_1990 = 2.7787%/yr. Compound annual growth of World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series COM (Comoros): 377,637 in 1984 to 433,103 in 1989 — the five years ending on the eve of the 1 January 1990 start date. See EconomyRecord::pop_growth_1990 in spheres-sim/src/data/mod.rs for why the window ends in 1989 and not with the single-year 1990 rate.

note: 1990 TECHNOLOGY: AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED. What this nation knew on 1 January 1990 is transcribed and sourced grant by grant, exactly like every other 1990 figure in this file, and is not read off tfp_trend - there was never a code path from the trend to the known set, and the zero that stood there was a claim about the world rather than an absence of one (BIBLE section 8 and iron rule 4, both amended 2026-08-30). THE PREDICATE IS SPLIT, and split by the technology's OWN EFFECT TYPE so that it is mechanically computable and never a per-nation judgement call. A node whose effects include MilitaryEfficiency, MilitaryStrength, DiffusionEmission or CostReduction is SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE: holding it means this nation could PRODUCE it, so operating an imported article does not qualify. Every other node is USE-SIDE: deployed and in operational use here is enough, whoever built it, because the effect such a node pays is a productivity, health or output effect and that effect is real in the country where the machine runs. Of the 48 technologies the tree lets anyone hold in 1990, 17 are sovereignty-side and 31 are use-side.

DATA-KEYED TAIL NATION. This nation is outside the 29 authored majors, so nothing here was authored technology by technology: a grant is made only where one of two named published global series supports it, and nothing is modelled, estimated or interpolated. A short list, or an empty one, is the correct outcome of that rule and not a gap in the work.

Data-keyed tail nation: not one of the 29 authored majors. Only the two series named in ruling 3 were consulted - WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 1990 and World Bank IT.CEL.SETS. Nothing was modelled, estimated or interpolated, and no other evidence was admitted. ISO3 key used for both series: COM.
WUENIC DTP3 1990 = 94% against the 80% UCI-1990 threshold: bio_universal_immunisation GRANTED.
IT.CEL.SETS at 31 December 1989 = 0 against a threshold of any positive count: refused.

The other 46 grantable 1990 technologies are BLANK for this nation by design, not by oversight: the 17 sovereignty-side entries are unreachable by any use-in-operation series, and no published global series was named that keys the remaining 29 use-side entries.

granted.source: WHO/UNICEF WUENIC DTP3 immunisation coverage (% of surviving infants), retrieved from the UNICEF public SDMX API, dataflow UNICEF:IMMUNISATION(1.0), indicator IM_DTP3, DATA_SOURCE field 'WHO/UNICEF estimates of national immunization coverage, 2025 revision'. Series value: COM, 1990 = 94%, at or above the 80% WHO/UNICEF Universal Childhood Immunization (UCI-1990) target that defines this technology's name.
